skill.name: azure-identity-ts
skill.description: Configure Azure authentication for TypeScript apps with the Azure Identity SDK, including DefaultAzureCredential, managed identity, service principals, and browser login.
skill.summary: Guide TypeScript developers through Azure Identity credential setup and common authentication flows.

content.value_statement: Azure authentication setup can be confusing across local development, cloud workloads, and service principals. This skill gives focused TypeScript examples for common Azure Identity credential flows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install @azure/identity for TypeScript projects.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and its credential chain order.
Provides examples for managed identity, service principals, and certificates.
Covers interactive browser login and device code authentication.
Shows token provider, sovereign cloud, and custom credential patterns.
limitations: It is reference guidance, not an executable authentication tool.
It does not validate Azure tenant, client, or subscription settings.
It does not create Azure resources or assign identity permissions.
It does not replace current Microsoft documentation for version-specific behavior.

use_cases.title: Set Up Local Azure SDK Authentication
use_cases.description: Use DefaultAzureCredential with Azure SDK clients during local development and deployment planning.

use_cases.title: Choose a Production Credential Strategy
use_cases.description: Compare managed identity, service principal, and workload identity patterns for Azure-hosted services.

use_cases.title: Document Azure Auth Patterns
use_cases.description: Create team guidance for credential options, token providers, sovereign clouds, and logging practices.

prompt_templates.title: Add DefaultAzureCredential
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an Azure SDK client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to add DefaultAzureCredential to a TypeScript Azure SDK client. Include the needed package and a short explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Select Credential Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare local and production authentication choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between DefaultAzureCredential, managed identity, and a service principal for my TypeScript app.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Managed Identity
prompt_templates.scenario: Use system-assigned or user-assigned managed identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript authentication pattern for managed identity. Explain when to use client ID or resource ID.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Credential Chain
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a custom credential chain for a TypeScript service that uses managed identity in Azure and Azure CLI locally.

output_examples.input: I need Blob Storage authentication for a TypeScript app.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends DefaultAzureCredential, describes local and deployed behavior, and identifies the Azure package to install.

output_examples.input: My service runs in Azure and should avoid stored secrets.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends managed identity and explains system-assigned and user-assigned identity options.

output_examples.input: I need a bearer token provider for an Azure API scope.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains how to pair DefaultAzureCredential with a token provider and the required service scope.

best_practices: Prefer managed identity for production services when Azure hosting supports it.
Use placeholders in examples and store real secrets outside source control.
Match credential choice to deployment environment and permission boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode tenant IDs, client IDs, client secrets, or certificates in application code.
Do not use interactive credentials for unattended production services.
Do not enable verbose Azure logging in production without reviewing sensitive output.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps configure Azure Identity authentication patterns for TypeScript and JavaScript Azure SDK applications.

faq.question: Does it run Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples. Any Azure CLI or PowerShell use is described as credential context.

faq.question: Which credential should I start with?
faq.answer: DefaultAzureCredential is usually the best starting point because it supports local and hosted Azure environments.

faq.question: Can it help with managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows system-assigned and user-assigned managed identity examples for TypeScript applications.

faq.question: Does it store secrets?
faq.answer: No. The examples use placeholders and recommend environment variables or managed identity instead of hardcoded secrets.

faq.question: Is it specific to Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: No. It can guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when generating Azure Identity examples.
